messages:
marta: heads-up — planning a small maintenance window tonight 02:00-03:30 UTC to run a preemptive IO-throttle probe on a handful of gpu nodes. goal: reproduce the intermittent nvme latency spikes seen last week and validate our graceful-drain behavior. will do rolling drains 4 nodes at a time across az pairs.

leo: sounds reasonable. what's the exact node set and backfill plan?

marta: node set = pool-gpu-a[120-127], pool-gpu-b[4-7] (total 12 hosts). backfill via hot-standby pool, we'll pre-warm kv-cache after each reboot. start order: az1 -> az3 -> az2 to minimize cross-region egress.

anya: do we have capacity headroom for that ordering? also cost impact if we shift traffic to burst racks?

marta: yes we ran a dry-run earlier today — ~18% free capacity in host-level scheduling. cost hit should be small (short window) but I put an estimate in the runbook: ~0.6% extra GPU-hours, see link: https://go/runbooks/infra/io-probe-2026 (internal).

chris: customer comms? any tenant-facing risk for Dedicated pools / reserved customers?

marta: none for reserved capacity tenants — this affects spot/intermittent pools only. still want SRE to post a heads-up to #support-ops in case someone hits a latency regression.

leo: can you paste the drain command you'll use? want to audit the taints/eviction grace for stateful tasks.

marta: sure — basic flow: `kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=15m` then `ssh node && sudo systemctl reboot` once kube shows pods rescheduled we run a KV seed: ```bash
curl -X POST https://internal-cache-seed/seed -d '{"pool":"gpu","range":"recent"}'
```

anya: KV seed time? if it's long we might expose cold-start regressions.

marta: seed target = 90s per node, we wait for telemetry: `cache.seed.ok` metric. if >3m we abort the next cohort and open rollback.

ops-bot: scheduled by marta: io-probe-maintenance @ 2026-03-15T02:00:00Z -> 2026-03-15T03:30:00Z. Runbook: https://go/runbooks/infra/io-probe-2026. Pager duty: infra-oncall.

chris: ok please include a short blurb for #customers-alerts: "No impact expected for reserved customers; intermittent pools may see transient latency while we validate mitigations." I'll copy edit.

leo: +1 to rollback guard. also let's enable lightweight tracing on the nodes during reboots so we can correlate NVMe lat spikes with kernel logs. `tcpdump` not needed, just `dmesg -w` capture and stack traces.

marta: added trace step to runbook. final ask: anyone object to the 02:00 UTC start? :alarm_clock:

anya: no objections. :thumbsup:

chris: approved. I'll push the support blurb in 30m. :eyes:

leo: i'll be on standby during the window.

marta: great — we'll kick at 02:00 UTC. leaving this thread open for last-minute notes.
